summary: Ahead of the Supreme Court's stray-dog review, the [Kerala, Goa and Jharkhand High Courts](#feature) pressed local bodies: no excuses for missing shelters, disciplinary action against defaulting officials, and a new suo motu case on dogs and cattle on highways.
The [Supreme Court](#courts) said future transfers of captive elephants must strictly follow its earlier directions, after five elephants were moved from Assam to Tamil Nadu temples in a hurry.
Objections to the [draft lab-animal rules](#movement) closed on 5 Nov amid a broad coalition calling for withdrawal; we found no official response yet.

OpenAI's [29 October Model Spec](#world) reportedly asks its models, for the first time, to weigh effects on animals. On the [EA Forum](#forum), Lotte de Lint explains why academia produces so little good evidence on cutting meat consumption.

cover.title: Stray dogs: High Courts turn up the heat before the Supreme Court's review
cover.dek: Acting on the Supreme Court's May 2026 directions, the Kerala High Court said local opposition is no excuse for failing to build shelters, the Bombay High Court at Goa ordered disciplinary action against officials who kept missing deadlines, and the Jharkhand High Court opened its own case on stray dogs and cattle on highways. The compliance reports feed a Supreme Court review reportedly listed for 17 November.

topStories.label: Draft lab-animal rules
topStories.title: Objections closed on 5 Nov; calls for withdrawal grow
topStories.text: Scientists, vets, MPs, actors and 60+ groups asked the Centre to withdraw G.S.R. 864(E). No extension or official response has been reported.

topStories.label: Supreme Court
topStories.title: No more hasty elephant transfers
topStories.text: The bench couldn't order five elephants returned to Assam, but said future transfers must strictly follow its directions.

topStories.title: OpenAI's Model Spec now mentions animals
topStories.text: Reviewers say the 29 Oct update is the first to ask OpenAI's models to weigh effects on animals.

feature.title: The High Courts are now enforcing the Supreme Court's stray-dog order
feature.dek: In its May 2026 judgment in the national stray-dogs case, the Supreme Court asked High Courts to monitor how states carry out its directions and report back. This fortnight, three High Courts showed what that looks like in practice. The [Kerala High Court](https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/kerala-high-court/kerala-high-court-joint-shelters-for-stray-dogs-panchayats-identify-suitable-land-556530) rejected excuses from local bodies, the [Bombay High Court at Goa](https://nenews.in/goa/goa-hc-orders-disciplinary-action-against-8-panchayat-secretaries-over-stray-dog-reports/70158/) went after individual officials, and the [Jharkhand High Court](https://www.thehansindia.com/news/national/jharkhand-hc-seeks-compliance-report-from-state-centre-over-stray-dogs-and-cattle-on-roads-1139521) opened a new case of its own.

items.text: Local bodies said they couldn't find land for shelters or faced resistance from residents. The bench said public opposition does not justify failing to comply, and defaulters risk contempt before the Supreme Court.
Two or three panchayats may set up a common shelter together.
Sterilised dogs removed from public premises must be released as the Supreme Court directed: not back into those premises, and not held in shelters in breach of the order.

Kochi Corporation must explain how it runs its ABC programme. Advocates Shruthi Bhat and Pooja Omanakuttan were appointed amici, and the Registry was to send a consolidated compliance report to the Supreme Court by 6 Nov.

The Bombay High Court at Goa noted "clear remissness", including by the Panaji Corporation, and told the Directors of Panchayats and Municipal Administration to start disciplinary action against officials who repeatedly failed to comply. Contempt remains possible separately ([Daijiworld](https://daijiworld.com/news/newsDisplay?newsID=1333598)).

Disciplinary proceedings were ordered against the secretaries of eight defaulting village panchayats, which get a final chance to report by 16 Nov. The Animal Husbandry Department now has until 1 Dec for a shelter action plan. The order date is inferred from the report.

Taking suo motu notice of road-safety risks from stray dogs and cattle on roads and national highways, the court sought responses from the Centre and the state and a compliance report. Next date: 3 Dec. The bench wasn't named in the report.

facts.text: In Re: Compliance with the Directions issued by the Supreme Court in SMWP (C) No. 5 of 2025 · W.P.(C) No. 23376/2026 · Dr. Justice A.K. Jayasankaran Nambiar and Justice Preeta A.K.

facts.label: Goa case
facts.text: Suo Motu Writ Petition No. 2 of 2026 (title as reported by [LiveLaw on 14 Oct](https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/bombay-high-court/goa-civic-officials-contempt-proceedings-delay-data-collection-554567)) · Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar

facts.label: Supreme Court
facts.text: Main judgment 19 May 2026, 2026 SCC OnLine SC 894 ([SCC Online summary](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/05/19/sc-stray-dogs-abc-rules-nationwide-sterilisation-directions-may-2026/)). A review of state-wise compliance is reported for 17 Nov; check the cause list.

facts.label: Not verified
facts.text: Outcomes of the Delhi (3 Nov), Madhya Pradesh (3 Nov) and Allahabad (affidavits due 5 Nov) High Court stray-dog hearings. We found no reports.

feature.whyItMatters: The Supreme Court's directions only matter if someone checks that municipalities and panchayats follow them. High Courts are now doing that, and they are naming officials rather than just issuing general orders. For advocates, these hearings are where to raise problems on the ground: missing ABC programmes, shelters that don't meet standards, or dogs released in breach of the order. The compliance reports going to the Supreme Court will also shape what it does next, so local evidence filed now can count.

cases.title: Supreme Court: captive-elephant transfers must follow the rules
cases.citation: Petition by People for Cattle in India (PFCI) · Supreme Court · CJI Surya Kant & Justice Joymalya Bagchi · hearing 5 Nov · case number not reported; linked to the pending captive-elephant case W.P.(C) 743/2014

parts.label: The ask
parts.text: PFCI challenged the transfer of five captive elephants from Assam to Tamil Nadu temples. Its counsel said one elephant was moved about 3,000 km in nine days, when the process normally takes around 50.

parts.label: Held
parts.text: All five had already been moved, so the bench said it couldn't order them returned now. It said future transfers must strictly follow the statutory requirements and its earlier directions on identity and ownership checks, and that High Courts and states can't act against those directions. PFCI withdrew, with liberty to apply in the pending case.

parts.label: Why it matters
parts.text: Long-distance transfers of elephants to temples have been hard to stop once under way. The bench's reminder gives advocates firmer ground to challenge the next one early.

cases.title: Madras: 87 illegal resorts in Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve to close
cases.citation: Dr. R. Karpagam v. Principal Chief Conservator of Forests & Chief Wildlife Warden · WP No. 13711 of 2022 · 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 527 · Madras High Court · Justices N. Sathish Kumar & G.K. Muthukumar · order date not stated

parts.label: The background
parts.text: The Erode Collector reported 87 resorts in the reserve, none with planning or building approval and no record of the hill-area authority permitting a change of land use.

parts.label: Directed
parts.text: All illegal buildings to be closed at once, with steps toward demolition; unlicensed resorts to be locked and sealed. Two resorts that got interim protection from another bench without disclosing this case were found not to have come with clean hands.

parts.label: Why it matters
parts.text: Tourism construction inside tiger reserves is a steady pressure on wildlife habitat, and this is an unusually sweeping order to undo it.

cases.title: Nahargarh sanctuary boundary dispute goes to the Rajasthan High Court
cases.citation: Rajendra Tiwari v. Union of India & Ors · Civil Appeal No. 13859/2026 · Supreme Court · CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana

parts.label: The ask
parts.text: An appeal from the NGT against revised boundaries of the Nahargarh Wildlife Sanctuary near Jaipur.

parts.label: Held
parts.text: The Court didn't rule on the merits and sent the appellant to the Rajasthan High Court, where the revised map is already under challenge. The High Court must consider all objections on how the reserve forest and sanctuary are identified. The bench also asked why a monitoring committee's report hadn't gone to the NGT.

cases.title: Madhya Pradesh: probe ordered into two more Kanha tiger deaths
cases.citation: Subit Chakraborty v. Union of India · WP 19398 of 2026 · Madhya Pradesh High Court (Jabalpur) · Chief Justice Alpesh Y. Kogje & Justice Vivek Jain · order date not stated

parts.label: Directed
parts.text: The state must investigate two further tiger deaths at Kanha Tiger Reserve and report within two weeks. Next hearing 16 Nov.

cases.title: Gujarat: town drops four-month meat shutdown
cases.citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Guj) 302 · Gujarat High Court · Justice Nikhil S. Kariel

parts.label: What happened
parts.text: Radhanpur Municipality had ordered slaughterhouses, meat shops and non-vegetarian restaurants closed for four months during a Jain leader's stay. In court it admitted there was no legal provision for this and said it would not press its 17 Aug decisions, so the petition was withdrawn with liberty.

parts.label: Why it matters
parts.text: Not an animal-welfare ruling, but a reminder that blanket meat closures need a legal basis.

justBefore.title: J&K High Court: cattle-theft FIRs don't justify preventive detention
justBefore.text: In Tariq Ahmad Dar v. UT of J&K (LPA No. 254/2026), Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani quashed a Public Safety Act detention based on cattle-theft FIRs, holding these were law-and-order matters that ordinary criminal law can handle. Reported 25 Oct; it continues this year's run of similar J&K rulings.

quiet: Unverified outcomes: the Delhi High Court stray-dog hearing on 3 Nov (MCD and NDMC sterilisation affidavits), the MP High Court stray-dog review on 3 Nov, the Allahabad High Court dog-bite hotspots matter (affidavits due 5 Nov) and the Madras High Court temple-elephant SOP listing on 30 Oct. We found no reports. LiveLaw's daily round-ups are partly paywalled, so a High Court ruling may have been missed.

Government: no new central notifications found from DAHD, MoEFCC, AWBI, the Central Zoo Authority, NTCA or WCCB, and no response yet to objections on the lab rules. Just before the window, the [Animal Feeds and Feed Ingredients (Quality Control) Order 2026](https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/10/16/animal-feeds-feed-ingredients-quality-control-order-2026-bis-certification/) made BIS certification mandatory (reported 16 Oct). FSSAI reportedly issued an approval letter on 27 Oct for a fermentation-derived mycelium ingredient, per a [vegconomist listing](https://vegconomist.com/category/cultivated-cell-cultured-biotechnology/approvals/); we couldn't confirm the details.
No NGT animal-law ruling found. Nothing new on the Kerala Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Bill, which the Centre told Parliament in August it could not accept.

Editor's notes: this issue covers 26 Oct – 8 Nov. No dated updates were found from ALPN, Vegan Outreach, Vegan India Movement, Mercy For Animals India, Veganuary India, Shrimp Welfare Project, Animal Ethics, One Just World, FIAPO, Animal Equality India or World Animal Protection India. PETA India's own site wouldn't load, so its items come from news reports. CALF and 'BIA' couldn't be identified with confidence and were skipped. The EA Forum mirror we normally use was down, so the forum section is built from the forum's own digests and is less complete than usual.

movement.tag: PETA India, Peedu's People and others · Draft lab rules
movement.title: Objections close on the draft lab-animal rules, with calls to withdraw them
movement.text: The comment period on the draft Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 864(E), gazetted 6 Oct) closed on 5 Nov, according to [MedBound Times](https://www.medboundtimes.com/daily-pulse/gsr-864-e-draft-animal-experimentation-rules-2026-objections) and most other reports. In the final days, scientists, vets, cross-party lawmakers and more than 60 groups demanded withdrawal ([Telangana Today, 3 Nov](https://telanganatoday.com/scientists-animal-welfare-groups-demand-withdrawal-of-draft-animal-testing-rules)), objecting to self-approval by in-house ethics committees, exceptions for wild-caught and stray animals, and inspections with advance notice. PETA India says more than 18,000 people and several actors and MPs back it ([OrissaPOST/PTI, 2 Nov](https://www.orissapost.com/?p=904809); PETA's own figures). Peedu's People joined a student march in Pune on 29 Oct ([Punekar News](https://www.punekarnews.in/?p=248065)), and former Assam opposition leader Debabrata Saikia filed a formal objection ([Sentinel, 26 Oct](https://www.sentinelassam.com/north-east-india-news/assam-news/assam-debabrata-saikia-seeks-withdrawal-of-animal-experiment-rules)). For the legal argument, read Shreya Bajpai's [LiveLaw piece](https://www.livelaw.in/articles/self-approval-another-name-2026draft-animal-testing-rules-pca-act-556696) (1 Nov), which says the draft fails Section 17 of the PCA Act and calls for targeted amendments. No extension or official response has been reported.

movement.tag: Humane World for Animals India · Stray dogs
movement.title: A training centre for Animal Birth Control staff opens in Lucknow
movement.text: UP's urban development minister opened the centre at Jarhara, set up by Lucknow Municipal Corporation and the AWBI and run by Humane World under a three-year agreement. It offers a 15-day course for vets, para-vets and dog handlers working on ABC programmes. The organisation calls it India's first such centre and says more than 100,000 Lucknow dogs have been sterilised and vaccinated since 2019; these are its own claims. Timely, given the courts' push on ABC compliance (see the [feature](#feature)).

movement.tag: Humane World for Animals India · Dog-meat trade
movement.title: 26 dogs rescued from a truck in Assam
movement.text: Police in Karbi Anglong stopped a truck carrying 26 dogs in sacks, suspected to be headed for the dog-meat trade. Local groups including JBF (Just Be Friendly) took part in the rescue and the dogs went to JBF's centre in Guwahati. The release mentions no FIR or legal sections. From the organisation's own press release.

movement.title: Plant-based meat beats chicken on absorbable protein in a lab study
movement.text: GFI India and CSIR-IHBT tested five commercial products with simulated digestion. Plant-based products showed 57–86% protein bioavailability against 21–43% for chicken. The authors note lab results don't show real-world absorption. The report also says India imports nearly 90% of its plant protein isolates, a gap for domestic industry.

movement.title: Fortified feed grew fish faster but didn't improve welfare
movement.text: FWI tested a fortified pellet feed against de-oiled rice bran on 12 farms in Nellore and in earlier pond and tank studies. Fish gained 73% more weight, but water quality, health and stress didn't differ, and about 45% of early-morning oxygen readings were below 3 mg/L whatever the feed. The feed also cost farmers more, so FWI won't build a programme on it. A useful negative result, published openly. FWI's [India grants call](#careers) closes 18 Nov.

movement.title: ACE's 2026 charity recommendations are out tomorrow
movement.text: ACE says it will announce its recommended charities on 10 Nov. This year's evaluations covered Aquatic Life Institute, Kafessiz Türkiye, Dansk Vegetarisk Forening, Sinergia Animal, Crustacean Compassion and Greener by Default; none is described as working in India. We'll cover the results next issue.

pick.label: Pick of the fortnight
pick.title: Takes on why academia underproduces high-quality evidence on reducing animal product consumption
pick.author: Lotte de Lint
pick.text: A Wageningen PhD researcher lists six ways academic incentives work against useful evidence on diet change. Studies often don't answer the questions advocates face, focus on health and climate rather than animals, and are concentrated in Western countries. Easy-to-test interventions crowd out more promising ones, and field data on real behaviour goes unrewarded. Of 637 outcomes in one library of studies, more than half measured intentions or attitudes rather than behaviour. For India, the point about Western-centred research is the key one: there is very little local evidence to design campaigns on.

posts.title: We tested 14 meat-reduction messages with real money at stake. Celebrities and history did best.
posts.author: Laura Thomas-Walters
posts.text: An online experiment with 4,761 Americans measured how much people valued a plant-based gift basket after short messages. The 'right side of history' and celebrity messages had the biggest effects; trend and pandemic messages barely moved anything. It measures one choice right after the message, not lasting diet change, and the sample is US-only.

posts.title: Votos Pelos Animais: How Farmed Animal Policy Wins Votes In Brazil
posts.author: JLRiedi (Faunalytics)
posts.text: A survey experiment with 1,908 Brazilian adults tested nine farmed-animal policy proposals. Banning destruction of the Amazon and Cerrado for industrial animal farming, and tougher penalties for mistreating farmed animals, won the most support; every pro-industry proposal fell below 50%. A similar study would be valuable for India's state elections.

posts.title: An ASI that's bad for animal welfare is probably bad for humans, too
posts.author: Michael Dickens
posts.text: Dickens argues that a superintelligent AI aligned with human preferences but harmful to animals is a narrow target: simply satisfying human preferences would also produce outcomes that are terrible for many humans. He concludes that getting AI values right matters for both. Pairs well with the [OpenAI Model Spec item](#world).

forum.alsoPosted: [Make diet change a Millennium Prize Problem for animal advocacy](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/TT9jF5corKdHgXXtz/make-diet-change-a-millennium-prize-problem-for-animal) by Pablo Moleman (we couldn't open it to summarise) · [The neglected layer of alternative proteins: institutional infrastructure](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/twpW7QancECxzbcAB) by Nadja Milivojev · Ariel Simnegar's [quick take on OpenAI's Model Spec](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/SYprbthckE7pcxPFz/ariel-simnegar-s-quick-takes?commentId=EAdxtd5FHewWuBM7A) (see [World](#world)). Our usual forum mirror was down, so dates and karma come from the forum's own pages and the [EA Forum Digest of 4 Nov](https://eaforumdigest.substack.com/p/ea-forum-digest-316).

careers.intro: Paid roles, grants and trainings that people in India can use, all checked as open on 9 Nov. Fish Welfare Initiative has three India openings this fortnight. GFI APAC is also hiring senior roles open across the region ([Head of Policy](https://gfi.org/resource/head-of-policy/)).

items.title: Grants for new ideas on farmed fish welfare in India
items.location: Open to anyone; the work must be relevant to Indian aquaculture
items.text: Standard grants up to ₹10 lakh, and up to ₹50 lakh for exceptional proposals. Academics, companies, NGOs and individuals can apply using FWI's template; basic research is funded only if it links to a possible FWI programme.

items.title: Understanding how people (actually) make decisions
items.location: Online (Google Meet) · 13:30 IST (08:00 UK) or 20:30 IST (15:00 UK) · 1 hr 30 min
items.text: A free, beginner-friendly introduction to behavioural science for campaigners, corporate relations and communications staff. It covers how people make decisions, the two systems of thinking, a framework for stronger messages and a few biases you can use straight away, with examples like winning a cage-free commitment or getting a petition signed. Registrants get a recording. The registration pages don't name an organiser, and the date and times come from the event details we were given, so confirm them when you register.

items.title: Strategic Advisor on Food Security
items.location: Remote, ideally in or near a focus region (including South/Southeast Asia), with regular overlap with CET hours
items.text: Leads ProVeg's food-security strategy in one region, steering protein growth toward plant-rich and alternative options. 30–40 hours a week, ideally a 12-month freelance contract.

items.title: Director of Digital Campaigns
items.location: Fully remote, anywhere (must be able to work legally where you live; no visa sponsorship)
items.deadline: End of day 30 Nov 2026 (time zone not stated)
items.text: Runs digital tactics such as mass emails, actions and creative assets in campaigns pressing food companies on farmed-animal welfare. Needs 3+ years' experience. Pay for non-US applicants is discussed at interview.

items.title: Sustainable Poultry Supply Chain Engagement Manager (India)
items.location: India, work from home with some travel
items.text: Persuades medium and large egg producers to switch to cage-free. Needs 2+ years in sales or similar and fluency in Telugu or Tamil; Hindi strongly preferred.

items.title: Welfare Measurement Lead
items.location: Indian nationals only · Eluru, Andhra Pradesh for at least 6 months of year one, otherwise remote within India
items.text: A senior role building FWI's welfare measurement and M&E systems, designing farm studies and managing 1–2 field staff. ₹1.3–2.7 lakh a month.

items.title: Human Resources Manager
items.location: Right to work in India required · remote, with a preference for time at the Eluru office
items.deadline: Rolling (the page mentions 15 Nov for earlier applicants)
items.text: Covers recruitment, employee relations, compliance and training, working with the Managing Director. ₹50,000–90,000 a month.

items.title: Centenary Research Award
items.location: Worldwide; lead applicant must be at a host research institute or organisation
items.text: Up to £250,000 for a 2–4 year project on a major animal-welfare challenge. Full proposals are due 15 May 2027.

items.title: OpenAI's Model Spec now asks its models to consider animals
items.text: OpenAI published an updated Model Spec, the rules its AI models follow, on 29 Oct. According to reviews by [Ariel Simnegar](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/SYprbthckE7pcxPFz/ariel-simnegar-s-quick-takes?commentId=EAdxtd5FHewWuBM7A) and [Zvi Mowshowitz](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec), the list of side effects models should weigh now includes effects on "other people, animals, or the environment". A new example has the model mention the breed's welfare problems when asked to find a Scottish Fold cat breeder, and another tells it to consider animals living in a park being redesigned. Simnegar calls it the first version to explicitly ask the models to weigh animal welfare. We couldn't open the Spec page itself to confirm the wording.

items.title: Cage-ban proposals missing from the Commission's 2027 work programme
items.text: The work programme published on 4 Nov doesn't mention the promised welfare laws on laying hens, broilers or pigs, the End the Cage Age commitments. The poultry proposal may still come in December 2026; no reason was given for the pig proposal.

items.title: Parliament bans permanent chaining of animals
items.text: On 28 Oct, Portugal's parliament passed bills banning permanent tethering, long-term confinement on balconies and restraint or training equipment that causes unnecessary pain. The law still needs presidential approval, then implementing rules within 90 days.

items.title: First cultivated beef approved, for pet food
items.text: Ivy Farm Technologies won approval on 5 Nov to sell cultivated Wagyu beef as a pet-food ingredient in the UK. Its applications to sell it as human food in the UK, EU and US are pending.
